title: imperfect hospital data through the nightly ingest
note: Written by hand from the harness's results (make imperfect-feed, tools/imperfect_feed.py); each finding names the runs (case/format) that show it.

findings.claim: a CSV export cut inside its last row: that lab result is served with its value cut short (6.5 for a two-decimal value) and no sample time; nothing counted, no error line, the night published
findings.expected: the cut row rejected and counted, or the file set aside; never a value short of its digits in the lake
findings.from: STD-025 (T-615a: a row the mapping cannot read is rejected and counted by reason); T-615b (a file that is not a readable CSV is quarantined)

findings.claim: an SS-MIX2 lab message cut inside OBX-5: the value is served cut short (6.5) with the sample time taken from the folder's date; counted only as 'OML-11:sample time from folder' in reader.json
findings.expected: the cut message set aside and counted (as an unreadable message is), never its cut value
findings.from: T-615a; the reader's own rule for a file it cannot read (PPR-01:quarantined in reader.json)

findings.claim: a CSV export that ends inside a quoted field (no closing quote): the last note is served cut short; nothing counted, the night published
findings.expected: the file set aside as not a readable CSV, or the row rejected and counted
findings.from: T-615b (not a readable CSV: quarantined); STD-025

findings.claim: a CSV row one field short is mapped with the missing column taken as empty: a lab result is served with no sample time; nothing counted
findings.expected: a row with fewer fields than the header rejected and counted
findings.from: STD-025; DATA-017 (the reader's row count is the export's)

findings.claim: a CSV whose header names the value column otherwise (result_val): all 200 lab results are served with no value; nothing counted, no error line, the night published
findings.expected: a column the mapping reads that is missing from the file refuses the table or holds the night with its name
findings.from: T-611 (a table that is not whole holds the night); mapping_check's column check before the first night

findings.claim: one chart number on two people's patient rows: the lake serves one patient with the second person's birth date and sex and the second person's visit; CSV and SQL count 'duplicate_keys 1' and publish; FHIR Bulk counts nothing
findings.expected: two different people under one key held for a person (the night held, or the key refused), never merged into one patient
findings.from: DATA-017 (a duplicate source key is counted; the last row wins) does not cover two people; T-659b (identity changes are a person's)

findings.claim: SS-MIX2: a second person's ADT-00 (another birth date and sex) in the same patient folder, newer: it replaces the first person's birth date and sex; nothing counted
findings.expected: an ADT-00 that changes birth date and sex of a patient said (counted, or held for a person)
findings.from: SS-MIX2 newest-wins (S22 3.1.2) is for corrections of one person; T-659b

findings.claim: a FHIR Bulk export with one cut-off line, a Big5 or UTF-16 file, or a UTF-8 byte-order mark: adapter run ends with a traceback (JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError) and the whole night fails; the audit and the steward's row say FAILED with the error's type only, no file or line
findings.expected: the bad line or file counted with its reason (or set aside, as the CSV reader does) and the rest of the export read
findings.from: T-615b (the CSV reader's quarantine); D-668 (a failure in words); the card's 'nothing crashes'

findings.claim: SS-MIX2: a diagnosis message in Big5 under MSH-18 ~ISO IR87 is read as Shift_JIS: its 標準病名 name is served garbled in the snapshot (code.text and display; the code is right); counted only as 'PPR-01:read as cp932' in reader.json
findings.expected: a message whose bytes do not read in its declared character set set aside and counted (as unreadable bytes are), never served garbled
findings.from: T-615b and D-215 (no guessed character set reaches a record); STD-020

findings.claim: a FHIR Bulk resource dated 0000-00-00 (an onset, or a birth date) fails the night's lake build: 'lake rebuild failed: ValueError: LAKE-BUILD: the lake could not build the snapshot ... the lake's log says where'; no row counted or named, nothing of the night served
findings.expected: the date refused and counted at the read, as the CSV path rejects it ('MappingError: unparseable date'), and the night goes on
findings.from: STD-025; DIN-012 (a placeholder is not a fact); D-669

findings.claim: rows rejected under 1 % of a table, and SS-MIX2 files set aside under 1 %, are counted only in completeness.json or reader.json: ingest_report.json has no error line, the audit event and the steward's batch row carry no rejected count, and the INGEST job's mail counts error lines only
findings.expected: each rejected row counted with its reason where a person reads the night (the report's lines, the steward's page)
findings.from: STD-025 (counted by reason); the card's 'each rejected row counted with its reason'; datacore DETAIL_KEYS

findings.claim: a FHIR Bulk export whose Observation file is zero bytes is published on a first night with no lab result at all; nothing counted, no error line
findings.expected: an empty or missing type of a bulk export held on a first night, as a CSV table is (T-611, NEW-DIN-8)
findings.from: T-611; NEW-DIN-8 (D-583: every table required on the first night)

findings.claim: a birth date after the patient's visits is served as written and counted nowhere in every format (F9 checks only a life longer than 122 years)
findings.expected: an impossible date left out and counted (as F9 does for 122 years), the patient kept

findings.claim: a FHIR Bulk onset 9999-12-31 is served as written and counted nowhere, where the CSV and SQL paths reject the same date ('DateRangeError: date <value>')
findings.expected: a FHIR export's dates held to the same range as a mapped source's
findings.from: DIN-012 (EARLIEST_YEAR, LATEST_YEARS_AHEAD in the mapping engine)

findings.claim: one person under two chart numbers (same name, birth date and sex) is served as two patients and FEAS counts 51 where the export holds 50 people; nothing tells a person that two charts look alike
findings.expected: the box keeps the hospital's two charts until a person merges them, and says which charts look alike so a person can
findings.from: T-659b (adapter pid-merge is a person's act); DATA-017

findings.claim: one CSV note longer than 131,072 characters sets the whole note file aside and holds the night ('not a readable CSV (field larger than field limit (131072))'); the SQL and FHIR paths keep the same note whole; the row is not named
findings.expected: the long note kept whole, or that row rejected and counted; never every note of the night set aside for one
findings.from: T-615b; STD-025 (a row, not the table)

findings.claim: a lab table without its sample-time column holds the night with 'validation error rate 4.76% exceeds 0.5%' (the number moves with the random sample); the reason names neither the table nor the missing column
findings.expected: the hold says which table lacks which column
findings.from: T-611; D-668 (a reason in words a person can act on)

findings.claim: a CSV row with one field more (a decimal comma) is rejected as 'MappingError: unparseable datetime <value>': the reason points at a date, not at the row's extra field
findings.expected: a row with more fields than the header rejected as such
findings.from: STD-025 (counted by reason)

findings.claim: a CSV file cut inside a multibyte character is set aside as 'the file mixes two character sets (line 151)': the file is cut short, not mixed
findings.expected: the reason says the file ends inside a character (a cut file)

findings.claim: a UTF-16 CSV with its byte-order mark is set aside as 'the file reads as UTF-16 without a byte order mark'
findings.expected: the reason says UTF-16 (with its mark) is not read

findings.claim: a second copy of a table under another name (lab (1).csv) is ignored with no word: a corrected file sent under a new name would be lost unseen
findings.expected: a file in the export folder that no table reads named in the night's report
findings.from: T-611 (what the export holds is said)

findings.claim: a FHIR Observation with a code the box does not know is served and counted nowhere; the mapped sources count such codes in unmapped_codes.json
findings.expected: unknown codes of a bulk export counted as a mapped source's are
findings.from: NEW-DIN-6 (D-580)
